implementation_notes: Swift checks conformance strictly but generates no forwarding: the proxy is a struct or class declaring the same protocol and implementing each requirement by calling the wrapped service, with the control logic inside those forwarders. Equivalence is thus explicit and compile-checked - a missing or re-typed requirement does not compile - while the forwarding surface is hand-maintained and grows with the protocol; for network services, and only within URLSession, Foundation's URLProtocol is the framework-level alternative.
pitfalls: Protocol extensions with default implementations let a wrapper omit a requirement without a compile error, silently dropping the control for that member.
Storing the service as an existential (any ServiceApi) hides properties the concrete type adds; keep the proxy internal when the concrete API still matters.
Mutating wrapper state from an async call needs actor isolation or a lock: a struct captured in an escaping closure mutates a copy, not the instance you hold.

variants.name: Foundation URLProtocol interception on a URLSessionConfiguration
variants.implementation_notes: For services reached through URLSession, URLProtocol is the interception hook: a subclass registered in URLSessionConfiguration.protocolClasses sees every URL load, so metrics, redaction, offline responses or redirection to a local proxy are added without changing the code that issues requests. Scope it to a dedicated configuration rather than the shared session, and remember that it covers URLSession traffic only - not other processes, not sockets.
pitfalls: URLSession.shared cannot be extended: the interceptor must be installed on a dedicated URLSessionConfiguration, so clients using the shared session stay uncontrolled.
The protocol must always finish the load (urlProtocolDidFinishLoading) exactly once: a missing or double finish hangs or crashes the loading system.
Interception is in-process only - other processes, raw sockets and non-URLSession stacks bypass it, so fleet-wide equivalence needs a sidecar instead.
